title: Investigate delayed cudaMallocAsync frees during continuous batching leading to KV-cache-backed memory accumulation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: In production continuous-batching workloads we observe steady GPU memory growth until OOM or forced eviction even though the KV cache size reported by the runtime is stable. Hypothesis: delayed frees from cudaMallocAsync (cross-stream) combined with our slab pooling and stream synchronization pattern cause memory to be held in CUDA arenas after the logical free, which prevents the driver from reusing memory for other allocations. This is amplified when KV cache shards/mutations create transient allocations on secondary streams during batched inference.

What we've observed:
- Telemetry: per-instance GPU resident memory climbs ~20-40 MB per minute under steady qps; token-level metrics and KV cache size (entries & bytes) do not increase.
- nvprof / nv-memstat snapshots show many allocations in the cudaMallocAsync arenas with "deferred free" timestamps aligned to stream sync events.
- Host stack traces show allocator->pool->defer_free paths; stream->fence ordering differs between older and newer driver/runtime combinations.
- Repro: synthetic harness that runs continuous batches (seq_len 1024, batch_size 8, request concurrency 12) reproduces growth within ~20 minutes on rtx-a6000.

Logs and artifacts: see attachments for heap snapshots, nvprof timeline, and memory flamegraphs.

Initial analysis and tradeoffs:
- Root causes considered: (A) cudaMallocAsync semantics + stream ownership delaying returns to OS; (B) our slab pool not merging small freed slabs back to superpages quickly; (C) KV cache eviction path allocating temporaries on non-default streams without explicit stream-ordered frees. Likely a combination.
- Short-term mitigations: force explicit cuMemFreeAsync synchronization on the allocation stream before returning resources to pool (adds latency and potential stalls), or fallback to cudaFree on problematic paths (worse perf).
- Medium-term: adjust slab pooling to use per-stream subpools with explicit deferred-free queues and periodic drain based on epoch or token watermark; ensure temp KV allocations use default stream or use stream-ordered callbacks to free into the correct arena.

Proposed next steps:
1) Add unit reproducer test in infra/harness with nvtx markers and configuration toggles for allocator mode (cudaMallocAsync vs cudaMallocAsync + immediate cuStreamSynchronize).
2) Instrument allocator to export per-arena deferred-free counts and last-free timestamps to console/console-traces for correlation with telemetry dashboards.
3) Try two experiments: A) force immediate cudaStreamSynchronize after KV write path to confirm the deferred-free correlation; B) switch small-temp allocations to host-pinned preallocated buffer (bypass cudaMallocAsync) to test if growth stops.
4) If experiment A confirms root cause, implement per-stream deferred-free queues that are drained on a background thread after stream callbacks instead of relying on driver timings.
5) Rollout plan: Canary changes (config flag) to runtime-1.20 canary hosts, monitor resident memory and latency P50/P95.

Acceptance criteria:
- No steady resident memory growth on reproducer for 2 hours at 3x baseline qps.
- No >5% regression in P95 generation latency with pooling changes enabled.

Related links and references:
- GitHub repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-mem-harness (link to branch ENG-13685)
- Console diagnostic dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/gpu-memory/ENG-13685
- Confluence writeup: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUN/pages/Memory+Hold+Behavior+ENG-13685
comments: 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial report filed after noticing steady growth on canary group. Attached nvprof timeline and sample logs. Marked P1 due to customer-facing OOM risk.

2026-03-13 - Marco Diaz: Reproducer built and running. Confirmed growth on my local with rtx-a6000. nv-memstat shows deferred frees clustered around stream callback intervals. Added nvtx markers to the request path for better correlation.

2026-03-13 - Priya Nair: Observed similar pattern in Dedicated cluster on runtime-1.19 with driver 525.89.02. Suggest checking driver differences; older driver on other hosts didn't reproduce as strongly.

2026-03-14 - Marco Diaz: Ran two experiments: (1) introduced cuStreamSynchronize after KV mutation -> memory growth stopped but latency P95 up ~8%. (2) switched temp KV allocations to preallocated pinned buffer -> growth stopped and P95 unchanged. Indicates allocator/stream interaction as primary cause.

2026-03-14 - Marco Diaz: Plan to implement per-stream deferred-free queue with streamCallback-based drains. Will open a draft PR and run canary. If that looks good, will gate behind runtime flag and roll out to canary cluster.
2026-03-14 - Design note (SRE): Add a one-off alert when resident memory increases monotonically for 15 minutes with KV size unchanged. Dashboard tile created (see attachments).
